changes.reason: Clarified that firm expenses may be paid from either or both treasuries; the draft wording could imply only London pays expenses.

answers.answer: Attrition uses simultaneous rolls: “roll one die for each held office card. Add one per fatigue on that card; Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire.” On retirement, “Move retiree to Pensioners, flip card into Vacant Offices, return its fatigue to supply.” Commanders have no office card and do not roll normal office attrition.

Only players who retired at least one pensioner select or discard one display card. They act “in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties: most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from PM.” The acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace a card during selection; if the display empties, skip all remaining eligible players immediately. Then discard all remaining cards and refill exactly three, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card. Return remaining Pensioners to their supplies.

At phase start check the opportunity marker; choose a main action once, or twice if the marker already matched it, then move the marker onto the chosen main action. Only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action after that; it is never doubled and does not move the marker. With at least four vacant offices, Enlist Writer places one additional writer once that turn, so if the marker allows a double Writer action, three writers total can be placed.
answers.evidence: Family; Family action table — Enlist Writer.

answers.answer: After all family actions, “if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one. Repeat while both remain.” With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order; pieces in Court are Company shares. “Seeking a share never pays family cash into Company treasuries.” The initial queue purchase is paid to the bank: an empty Stock Exchange space costs £2, £3, £3, £4 or £5.
answers.evidence: Family action table — Seek Share; New Company shares.

answers.answer: Fill vacancies in ascending number on their card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate; on promotion, transfer fatigue to the new card and insert the old vacant card into ascending hiring order. Hiring own family requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. If no candidate exists or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

The former Chairman announces how many shares are needed for a pure majority (more than half the current shares); shareholders may campaign and the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one winning Company share into the Chairman slot and give that player the title marker. It remains a Company share for dividends, majority and scoring, but “cannot be traded or invested in firms.” If nobody reaches the majority, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself; this fallback needs no Nepotism consent.

For a Company-office check, first commit resources and cash; all check cash comes from the acting office treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, and roll using the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office’s actions, returns its officeholder to supply, discards fatigue and flips the card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm procedures can modify this. Do not take a dead action with no effect or success chance, such as trade with no ship or Deploy without dice merely to trigger officer losses.

The Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 to Balance. Each additional advance needs consent of players controlling a majority of Company shares (counting the Chairman), and Debt may never pass the track end. Then allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, lowering Balance by each transfer; borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while respecting the borrowing limits. Cash already in offices stays there.

Manager of Shipping must spend treasury until £2 or less remains. The Manager may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without its owner’s consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China if that office exists; extra ships serve only until Refresh.

The President declares regions for Trade, including the home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 of that President’s treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. A failed check can be retried during operations if affordable, and each President may have at most one successful Trade per turn; failed attempts/retries stay within that President’s uninterrupted opportunity. Successful capacity is one order per ship in that Presidency’s sea zone and ships do not exhaust. Fill as many orders as possible in declared regions: first writer to home port, then each order must extend the route filled during this same Trade. Writers from another Presidency cannot extend it; use all available writers and then filled-order tokens for remaining ships, which continue the route. No President may fill another President’s home region even if vacant. Company Balance gains each order’s printed value, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it that turn; President gets £1 per order and each writer owner gets £1 per placed writer.

A Commander may target their Presidency’s home, any associated region, or a region bordering an associated region, but not another home region or another Presidency’s Company-controlled region. A Company region is a legal target only if it has unrest or a closed order, so Deploy can have an effect. Exhaust officers and regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice; subtract the combined strength of the target and every other region in its empire, counting the target only once (Company-controlled defense strength is zero). After every attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments have no officer-loss roll.

On success, take from the bank £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot modifier, with a minimum equal to surviving officers used in this attempt plus one for the Commander. Count only this attempt’s surviving participating officers and used regiments/alliances. Pay repeated cycles: £1 for Commander plus £1 for each of their used surviving officers; then £1 per used surviving officer of each other family clockwise; then £1 per used regiment and each used alliance piece to the bank, regardless of alliance strength. Repeat from the Commander until loot is gone. The Commander gets one trophy per target tower. Then remove target tower and dome (and every matching empire flag if it was a capital), open all target orders, remove all unrest, and on new conquest put the loot/control token region-symbol-up above its associated President’s box, Governor overlay in the conquered region, and only Governor card in Vacant Offices. If Elephant faced outward, move it fully inside. Catastrophe returns half the Commander family’s trophies rounded up, returns Commander to supply, and exhausted officers still check losses; there is no office card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Actions — Commanders and Deploy; successful control table; catastrophe paragraph.

answers.answer: Take the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces that pool by one regardless of result. A success pays £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, and then chooses exactly one: build one stage of a Company ship; commission a regiment into the Army associated with the Governor’s President; or add an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President’s treasury. A ship build success places a partial ship if none is there, or completes an existing partial ship into that President’s associated sea zone, requiring two successes total. Each unsuccessful roll adds one regional unrest, and catastrophe also removes the officeholder normally. Each tax after the first this turn adds regional unrest. Repeat with the shrinking pool until the Governor stops, dice run out or catastrophe occurs.

Company expenses reduce Balance by £1 per existing Debt, each officer or regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones including China; Commanders are excluded. If Balance is short, take £5 emergency loans: each advances Debt one only if a track space remains, and at maximum Debt keep taking loans without further Debt advance. New emergency Debt adds no current-turn expense. After loans set Balance to zero; one or two loans lower Standing one, three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations at current Standing; if below, lower Standing one. Last, the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends at one cash per Company share, paying each owner £1 per share including the Chairman. If total cash paid in dividends is strictly greater than expectations, Standing advances one.
answers.evidence: Revenue — Company expenses, expectations and dividends.

answers.answer: A Company-directed Invasion or Rebellion has its primary Crisis resolved first, then secondary Rebellions in other Company regions with unrest, in Bombay, Madras, Bengal Army order; within each Presidency its Commander chooses its associated regions’ order. Primary normal Crisis strength is normal Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in the target; primary Foreign Invasion uses only the ordinary attack die; each secondary Rebellion uses only the number of unrest cubes there, with no event modifier or empire strength. For defense, the associated Commander chooses and exhausts pieces; if vacant, Military Affairs acts instead, or if both offices are vacant the Chairman chooses. The actor exhausts active Army pieces equal to Crisis strength, or as many as possible; an alliance’s printed strength is usable once and cannot be split. If newly exhausted strength equals Crisis strength, attack fails and defense succeeds: remove all unrest in the attacked region and Commander gains one trophy; if this defeats a normal primary Invasion, also remove an attacker tower if possible. If it does not equal, attack succeeds and defense fails, causing Region Loss (and empire growth for a successful primary Invasion). Whether a strength-2 alliance successfully defends a strength-1 attack remains explicitly unresolved in the summary; do not assume how excess indivisible strength counts.
answers.evidence: Events — Attacks on Company; Mounting defense table; unresolved counting boundary.

answers.answer: A result of −1 or less fails: discard the law, resolve a dilemma’s “If Failed” text, and the Opposition Leader returns the token and takes the PM dial. The new PM moves the proposed policy one adjacent space either direction and resolves that policy. At zero or more, the law passes: place it with passed laws, PM takes the passed-law token, resolve the selected policy, then immediate law effects. Finally restore all voting cards to regular orientation after either outcome. If a law causes Company failure, finish voting before Final Scoring.

In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call the special vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Use ordinary voting procedure and support threshold, but there is no accompanying policy and PM may vote against it. On pass, lower Debt one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, give PM a passed-law token and activate firms. On failure, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping/placing the Court VP token up to a maximum of ±3 VP per share; PM stays in power and the Deregulation law is not discarded. 1813 starts deregulated.

After Family share creation and before Hiring, investments occur in any order until players wish no more; a manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm and PM between firms. To form a firm, a player who manages none returns one eligible Company share to supply or flips a workshop to invested, flips their board to firm-charter side, places a family member as first firm share, sets Value to its leftmost space and takes £5 from the bank into London. Investing, with manager consent, contributes an eligible Company share or workshop to create one firm share and takes £5 from the bank into London. No more than ten shares can be created; beyond the cap investment still contributes £5 without a share. Cannot use the Chairman share, Company shares while Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, or a share created this turn even if traded away. Invested workshops never revert and give neither bonus nor Company-failure VP, even if firm fails.

Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn; only a firm with at least one ship may choose trade, including a closed home port, and its selected home port must be open when filled. Managers secretly and simultaneously choose strategy and bid from London; bids reveal simultaneously, while strategies stay facedown until their Presidency begins. At the start of that Presidency, before other actions, reveal matching strategies, roll one die per £1 bid and pay bid to bank; at least one 1 or 2 permits trade. Initiative is ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s), possibly negative. President’s successful Trade creates initiative the same way; after it succeeds, fill lowest initiative first and President sets tied order. If President vacant or does not succeed, firms fill after Commander/Governors, with Chairman choosing ties. Firm fills only open orders, up to ships + 1, starting at home port and tracing its own filled route; it cannot refill its own earlier order but may refill a different firm’s or Company’s order. Previously filled order pays half listed revenue rounded down. Revenue goes to India treasury; advance Value one space per full £6 added there this turn.

At start of Revenue before the Company, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of their share count or Value, using either or both treasuries. After expenses, manager may pay dividends from India treasury only: each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 manager. Waiving a shareholder’s payment requires both that shareholder’s choice and manager consent; they may forgo any number of shares on any dividend. Record total actual cash paid out, not per-share dividend; active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero and Hobnob keeps its previous marker. Sweep remaining India cash into London. If unable to pay expenses, dissolve unless rescued: shares go to Debtor’s Prison at −1 VP each, ships to matching shipyards, charter flips to family side; workshops remain invested. Rescue may be emergency investment under normal Company share/workshop rules (even at ten-share cap), paying expenses, losing remaining cash and lowering Value one per emergency investment, or an emergency negotiated merger with only one other firm, every involved shareholder consenting; that other firm must first pay its own expenses, then cover the endangered firm’s unpaid expenses.

Components are limited, and when a supply runs out complete as much as possible; cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. All information, including discards and family cash, is public except facedown blackmail and firm strategies/bids while selection is underway.

Negotiable items are enterprises, facedown blackmail, family treasury cash, Company or firm shares, and promise cards. Officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial and Chairman piece may not be traded. To transfer a share, return the old owner’s family member and replace it at the share’s location with a member from the receiving family; adjust VP when luxury ownership changes. Played faceup blackmail cannot be traded.

Immediate transfers are binding; promises of future behavior are nonbinding, except a printed promise card’s guaranteed effect may be called if possible. Calls follow that card’s timing and limits, and no promise calls occur during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, the guarantor chooses which to fulfill. Transferred resources cannot activate twice; for example, a workshop paid in Bonuses does not pay again after being sold during that same phase.

Use the chosen scenario’s player setup cards and “add three extra cards for five players or six for six players. Shuffle and deal evenly.” Place every listed holding: cash and enterprise cards go to player areas; put each office family member in its office and give its office card to its owner; Company share members go in Court; writers, officers, trainees and Commanders go in indicated boxes (Commander has no office card); take each shipyard with its ship in the listed sea zone or on the shipyard if unfitted. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. For the London display, shuffle prestige and blackmail together as one deck; deal three, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown.

The game ends after the scenario’s final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Failure is normally immediate; if it occurs during Events in India, finish that phase, and if legislation causes it, finish the vote before scoring. Once game over, stop negotiations, promise calls and blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use; during all Final Scoring, no negotiations or promise calls are allowed.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions — end and failure.

answers.answer: Power counts enterprises and Company shares at their current Power-track rates (bottom two positions zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, two for PM and printed card power, including faceup or facedown blackmail and applicable spouse. Most/second awards are 3/1 VP if final turn 1–3, 5/2 if turn 4–6, and 8/4 if turn 7–8. Tied first players receive only the lower award each and there is no other award; tied second receive none. Highest final VP wins; ties go to most windows, then clockwise from PM.

If Company survived, add Court’s current VP value per Company share; if it failed, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. Final company outcome: after survival, roll office attrition and retire Pensioners with no display cards; after failure, instead draw one random Company failure card. Deregulated firm scoring and the firm special retirement happen earlier in either outcome: score each player’s firm shares (round their own total down once, then deduct one per their family piece in Debtor’s Prison), then let eligible shareholders retire one member from supply before Power. Prizes, luxuries and spouse points generally are already recorded when gained/lost.

Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Make required enterprise/share trades immediately upon taking a spouse. Retirement discounts can stack and are personal; each discount is usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring. Discounts reduce actual spending, and thus London display-selection priority.
answers.evidence: London Season — spouses and returned shipyard rule.

answers.answer: If a shipyard is returned because of Violet Effingham or unpaid tax, its fitted ship stays in play. That shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship remains in play; it becomes purchasable after that ship returns.

Enlist Writer places a member in any Presidency Writers box; with at least four vacant offices, add one extra writer once this turn (a doubled action can place three total). Enlist Officer puts a member in Officers-in-Training. Luxury costs £4 to the bank and gives a luxury, 2 VP while owned, a window icon and social enterprise status. Shipyard costs £2 to bank, gives its matching ship unfitted on the yard, and is a Shipping enterprise worth one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. Workshop costs £5 to bank, gives a manufacturing enterprise worth two votes and £1 bonus, and is worth 1 VP if Company fails unless invested. Seek Share pays the bank for an empty Stock Exchange spot at £2, £3, £3, £4 or £5 and creates an applicant, not yet a share.

If a required family piece is unavailable in supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize’s printed VP; this also applies when creating a firm share. If no Family action is possible, take none and return the opportunity marker to supply.
answers.evidence: Family — forced piece reuse; no-action rule.

answers.answer: If Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns. Place a member from supply or, if necessary and possible, take one from a prize and lose that prize VP. If this is impossible, there is no Chairman.

The Chairman hires Director of Trade by choosing a current officeholder other than Chairman/Governor, or any writer if all offices are vacant; Commanders are not officeholders. Chairman chooses any writer as Manager of Shipping; for Military Affairs, a Presidential Commander, or if none any officer, or if none any Officer-in-Training. Director chooses a President from a writer of that Presidency or Governor associated with that Presidency. The associated President chooses a Governor from a writer or officer in the region; a Commander is not an officer and is ineligible. Chairman chooses any writer for China Superintendent, immediately upon China’s creation. Governor General replaces Director and is hired the same way. Own-family hiring requires verbal consent from every other player represented in candidate pool except Chairman elections and Commander appointments.
answers.evidence: Hiring — Office hirers and candidates; Nepotism.

answers.answer: Director may make repeated Special Envoy checks, paying £1 from treasury per die and taking no penalty. Each success either opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China: place its Superintendent overlay/card and Chairman immediately hires a writer. After all Envoys, Director may make up to two transfers, each moving one writer or ship between any Presidencies or sea zones (including China once created); transfers cannot happen while Envoys continue.

Military Affairs may make up to two transfers, each moving an officer or regiment from one Army to another while it remains in the top half. Then assign every Officer-in-Training to any Army’s top half. Finally appoint Commanders: if the slot is vacant or another family has more total pieces in that Army than incumbent’s family, choose among families with the most pieces, move chosen officer to Commander slot and return old Commander to the top as officer. A tie with incumbent family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.

Each President chooses the order of their Commander, Governors and own Trade; each position must get an opportunity, though Commander/Governors may decline. Each finishes all actions before the next begins, and Trade cannot interrupt another position. If President is vacant, Chairman sets order only and cannot Trade or approve local-alliance purchases.
answers.evidence: Company Operation; Presidency operations and Trade.

answers.answer: Successful Trade does not exhaust ships. At Refresh, writers on orders return to their associated Presidency Writers box, using dividers to preserve affiliation; filled tokens and Presidency dividers return to supply.

At the start of Commander operations, before Deploy, request funds from the President’s treasury for printed-price local alliances in the Army; President must approve. Move purchased alliances to top/active half. When used for Deploy or defense, exhaust the whole alliance to bottom; its printed strength is usable once and cannot be split among purposes. Refresh exhausts any unused active alliances and does not reactivate alliances as it does officers/regiments.

For Deploying in an already Company-controlled region to reopen orders or clear unrest, Company defense penalty is zero and no tower trophies are gained. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, take the minimum loot: surviving participating officers used in this attempt plus £1 for the Commander, and distribute it normally.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy — already Company-controlled region.

answers.answer: Each successful Governor Build performs one ship stage. If the Governor’s region has no partial ship, that success places it there; if one is already there, the success completes it into the sea zone associated with that Governor’s President, so two successes are needed total. A partial ship has no other effect. A successful Commission regiment places it in the Army associated with the Governor’s President; it has officer-like strength, loot is paid to bank, and it does not cause officer-loss rolls.

China is created by a successful Envoy or Envoy to China law; in either case Chairman immediately hires any writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping and Director may send ships there like any sea zone; China ships count as Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws. China acts after Bengal.

After Bengal, China may make one Trade attempt only, including a failed one, so it cannot retry. Roll one die per ship. If Company-controlled regions have no export icon, do not attempt Trade. On success, count icons only in all Company-controlled regions: Company Balance receives £4 times the number of icons; Superintendent family receives £1 per icon from bank. Non-Company exports count for neither payment; Company payment is not a flat £4.

When Governor General law creates the office, make all Governors pensioners immediately, remove their overlays and partially built Company ships, and return Governor/Director cards to the box. Replace Director with Governor General, preserving holder and fatigue, and place its ribbon overlay. Governor General hires Presidents and uses Director’s treasury and turn position, is hired like Director and rolls attrition normally. Later conquests create no Governors or overlays; printed Company symbols show control. When Company regions are lost, skip Governor Elimination.

Governor General first adds £3 to Balance per Company region. It may then repeatedly Govern, paying £1 treasury per die with no penalty. Every rolled 6 adds one unrest to every Company region, even on success; failure adds another unrest to every Company region. On success, add £1 per Company region and choose one benefit per region: complete a Company ship into any sea zone including China; place a regiment into any Army; or add £2 to Balance or any office treasury except its own, while adding unrest to a Company region. If multiple Tax choices occur this turn, their unrest must be placed in different regions. At most one successful Govern per turn.

First roll storm die; resolve required storms before drawing any event. A sea-zone result checks that zone, three storms checks every sea zone, and no storm indication means no checks. Company and extra ships are exempt; check player-owned ships in Company fleets in affected zones; China ships count Eastern; firm ships count in strategy zone; Hobnob ships are exempt. Roll once per eligible ship: 1–2 nothing, 3–4 fatigue or sink if already fatigued, 5–6 sink. Return a sunk ship to its shipyard unfatigued.
answers.evidence: Events in India — sequence; Storms table and procedure.

answers.answer: When an order closes, return any writer on it to its owner’s supply; flip a filled token to closed. If a close is directed at a region whose orders are already all closed, Cascade by closing every open order directly connected to those orders. If a connected order is already closed, instead close that region’s northernmost open order; if none are open, it also Cascades. A region initiates a Cascade only once per event tile, but it can receive effects from multiple Cascades.

Turmoil closes the northernmost open order in the top-stack region; if all are closed, it Cascades. Windfall owners take £1 per writer on orders in the top-stack region and each bordering region. Shuffle moves Elephant, shuffles that tile with the remaining draw stack, then separately shuffles discards and places them on top; if the draw stack is empty, March last instead.
answers.evidence: Events in India — event procedure table.

answers.answer: Leader gives a top-stack sovereign region one tower. If dominated, it instead rebels with the printed explosion modifier. Move Elephant only if it was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.

Peace on a border opens orders connected across Elephant’s border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant is wholly inside a region, instead open all orders there and remove its unrest. Then Elephant Marches in either case.

For an Invasion Crisis, compare the sovereign attacker’s whole-empire strength plus event modifier with the defender’s whole-empire strength; attacker must be strictly greater, so equality does not win. Success replaces defender’s flag with attacker’s dominated flag; taking a capital shatters its empire. If attacker had no empire, use a free capital/star and matching small flag; if none are available, no new empire/flags form. Failure removes one tower from attacker.

For non-Company Rebellion, compare only the rebelling region’s strength plus modifier to its sovereign capital’s strength; other regions of the empire do not count, and attacker must be strictly greater, so equal is failure. On success actor becomes sovereign, removes its flag and closes all its orders (Cascade if already closed). On failure remove one tower from the capital.

On Region Loss, Commander returns half their family’s trophies rounded up, then Commander member returns to supply. Roll once per officer in associated Army and remove each officer on a 6. Eliminate Governor and return its card to unused stack, fatigue and member to supply; remove overlay, partial Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion specified strength) and appropriate invasion flag; return control token to its region with £ loot side down and region-symbol side up. Future conquest gets no loot modifier and region loses Presidency association. Invasion Crisis closes all orders or Cascades if already closed; Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss equals regions lost so far this turn: first −1, second an additional −2, etc. If failure results, finish India Events. A lost region does not automatically cause loss of another; resolve each attack and defense separately.

After a successful Invasion Crisis, Elephant moves to the successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); otherwise it moves to the top-stack region. In a Company region place it fully inside; in a dominated region point toward its sovereign; in a sovereign region point across the tile’s shape-marked border. If that neighbor is already dominated by actor, use the first clockwise neighbor that is not; if all are dominated, use the redirect-arrow border pointing toward empire capital.

Foreign Invasion rolls storm die for targets: West means Bombay, South Madras, East Bengal; all storms means each, and none means top-stack region. For each target, roll ordinary die for attack strength and resolve Invasion/Company attack. On success close all target orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove target flag and all matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, and set tower strength to half attack roll rounded down. March with circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside an invaded Company region. The FAQ clarifies unrest does not add to attack strength or determine resulting tower levels.
answers.evidence: Events — Foreign Invasion; FAQ & Rulings — Foreign Invasion and unrest.

answers.answer: PM must draw at least one law, one at a time. After one or two ordinary non-dilemma draws PM may stop or draw up to three total, then chooses one revealed law and discards others. Drawing a dilemma forces its selection and immediately ends drawing. Before voting, PM turns dial clockwise or counterclockwise and stops at the first policy space matching the chosen law’s bottom icon; that space determines target and consequence.
answers.evidence: Parliament — law draw and policy selection.

answers.answer: Tax makes each family pay £1 to bank per target it owns; unpaid targets return to supply, including Chairman if taxed. Fitted ship of a lost shipyard stays in play, and yard cannot be bought until ship returns; losing prize/luxury removes VP. If policy includes windows, additionally pay each window on enterprises and family-member prizes, returning unpaid enterprise/prize member. Bonus means bank pays each family £1 per target owned. Power swaps target Power marker with next higher marker; if already highest, swap any other pair.

Starting with PM and clockwise, each £1 family cash buys a vote plus printed card votes. A card’s votes can be used only once in the entire vote across all rounds: rotate when used and leave rotated until resolution, so it cannot vote again in a later round. Adjust support up/down; tracks unlimited. PM may call another full round or stop after each, but a round with no votes ends voting.

A player who voted for may later oppose, but after opposing cannot vote for in this vote. Track opposition; the player with most opposition holds Opposition Leader, while a tie leaves token with its current holder. With recipient consent, votes may be cast on behalf of someone who already opposed or commits to oppose; add them to that person’s opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except when forced to use “Vote with my enterprises” promise.

Pay printed upkeep separately for every family member on a prize even on the final turn. If unpaid, return that member and lose the prize’s printed VP. On final turn, do upkeep but skip Refresh and go to Final Scoring. Otherwise return writers to their associated Presidency Writers box (dividers preserve affiliation), return filled tokens and dividers and extra ships to supply, reactivate exhausted Army officers/regiments, exhaust active local alliances without reactivating them, keep fatigue on fitted player ships, then advance turn marker and begin London Season. Trade itself never exhausts ships.

Each shareholder may retire one extra member per London Season from supply rather than Pensioners, regardless of firms owned. Actual cash spent after spouse discounts cannot exceed the highest total dividend marker among firms in which they own a share; printed prize cost may be higher if discount covers difference. No retirement from a firm with absent or zero marker. Otherwise retirement is normal, including prestige eligibility. At start Final Scoring, first score firms, then allow one special retirement regardless of Company survival/failure, before Power or any ordinary final scoring; no display cards are used in Final Scoring.

A firm has London and India treasuries. Investment cash is £5 from the bank to London; London pays for ship acquisition and bids, and can pay expenses. Trade proceeds go to India; India pays dividends and may also pay expenses. Firm expenses may be paid from either or both treasuries; after dividends, remaining India money is swept to London. Family cash cannot move into or out of firm treasuries. London cannot buy equity shares: creating shares requires contributing a Company share or workshop.

Firms phase happens after Family share creation and before Hiring. Investments happen without set order until no one wants more; manager resolves timing conflicts within their firm and PM resolves conflicts between firms. Then managers choose strategies.

A firm may fit a ship from its own or another player’s shipyard, but must have that owner’s consent and pay £3 from firm London treasury to bank. It may buy a player-owned ship already in Company with owner’s consent: £3 if unfatigued or £2 if fatigued, paid into Shipping treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships.

Only a player who manages no firm at all may initiate a hostile takeover; managing another firm makes them ineligible. Get consent of holders of a majority of target shares, then move target firm’s ships, money and shares to own charter and copy both cube positions. Former manager takes back cubes and flips board to family side.

For a merger, managers negotiate and every shareholder must consent. Highest-Value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among tied firms. Move all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. Share transfers may be negotiated. If primary would exceed ten shares, return excess shares to their owners’ supplies, with those owners’ consent. It is one binding immediate transfer; primary’s value/dividend track remains.

Hobnob entails no bid, trade or dividends, but the firm still pays expenses and retains its previous dividend marker for retirement. Firm ships face storms in strategy zone, except Hobnob ships are exempt.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies; firm expenses and dividends.

answers.answer: Emergency investments follow normal Company-share/workshop rules even when the firm is at ten shares and no new share can be created: eligible Company-share/workshop contribution still invests £5 from bank to London and pays expenses. After each emergency investment, lose any remaining cash and lower Value one space. Same-turn shares cannot be invested even if traded away, and Chairman share or Company shares while Standing and/or Debt is lined are ineligible.

Emergency negotiated merger may involve only ONE other firm, and normal merger procedure still applies, including consent of every involved shareholder. The other firm must first pay its own expenses if it has not already done so, then cover the endangered firm’s unpaid expenses.

Voluntary dissolution requires every shareholder’s consent and uses insolvent-firm dissolution: shares go to Debtor’s Prison at −1 VP each, ships return to matching shipyards, charter flips to family side. Workshops stay invested for the rest of game.

During final scoring, for each player separately add VP from all shares across all their firms and round that player’s total down once, then deduct 1 VP per their family piece in Debtor’s Prison. Per firm share, Value 1 is −1 VP, 2 is 0, 3–4 is ½, 5–7 is 1, 8–9 is 1½, and 10 is 2. Separately, if Company survived, add current Court VP per Company share; if it failed, subtract that share value and add 1 VP for each uninvested workshop.
answers.evidence: Scoring — final scoring order; firm-track VP; Court/workshops.

answers.answer: Per family member, the prize table is: cost £2, upkeep £0, 0 VP, 0 windows; £4, upkeep £1, 2 VP, 1 window; £8, upkeep £2, 4 VP, 2 windows; £14, upkeep £3, 8 VP, 3 windows; and £20, upkeep £4, 12 VP, 4 windows.

The standard scenario table gives 1710 turns 1–5 and no deregulation procedures; 1758 turns 3–7 and can vote in deregulation; 1813 turns 5–8 and begins deregulated; Long 1710 turns 1–8 and deregulation is available separately.

1710 starts at £10 expectations/0 Debt, each office treasury £3, Royal Protection, one regiment per Army and no Company ships. 1758 starts at £12 expectations/3 Debt, each office £4, Calico Acts, one regiment per Army and one Company ship in East Indian; put Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.

1813 starts turns 5–8 with £10 expectations/0 Debt, £3 in each office, Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor’s Prison side), Calico Acts, two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Put +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China, put Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in their Presidencies, return Governor General law to box and place its office overlay over Director of Trade. Use Governor General instead of Director and no Governors; map comes from scenario card reverse.
For final turns 1–3 the Power awards are 3 VP most and 1 second; turns 4–6 are 5/2; turns 7–8 are 8/4. If tied for first, each tied player gets only the lower award and no other award.

Initial Power positions are Social 2, Company shares 1, Shipping 0 and Manufacturing 0. Deregulation Standing £4/£6/£8 and Debt 5/6/7/8 spaces are lined; Standing £4 and Debt 8 are starred. Standing expectations run £4/6/8/10/12/14/16, and reset S is above £10.
answers.evidence: Setup — Power positions and Standing/Deregulation spaces.

answers.answer: No. The FAQ says unrest does not add to Foreign Invasion’s primary attack strength or determine its tower levels: use the ordinary die both as attack strength and to halve into towers. On success, close target region’s orders once; if already all closed, Cascade. Region Loss does not close them again.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings — Foreign Invasion and unrest.

answers.answer: If Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reduces a check to zero dice, that is failure. Company Fraud is at start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice the highest roll (minimum zero), and take from bank only the amount actually removed from Balance. Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to vacancies. Military Oversight demotes one Commander to officer, then appoints a Commander from officers; the same former Commander remains eligible to become Commander again. These are card-specific corrections, not changes to normal check/hiring rules.

At common setup, set Company Balance £5, family VP markers to zero, shuffle events and put local alliances in their named Army boxes; loot tokens start money-side up in matching regions. Use the chosen scenario card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and India political map. Set Turn marker on its date and PM dial arm to matching date; the scenario determines final turn.

Each turn is London Season → Family → Firms (if deregulated) → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. Skip London Season on the game’s first turn. Eligible special Deregulation votes occur at very start of turn, before London Season.

If Chairman office is vacant, the former Chairman starts retirements. Proceed clockwise; each player may retire each Pensioner to a prize, paying its printed cost, moving member to prize and gaining printed VP. Set actual spending aside until London Season ends to establish display order, then pay bank. Unused Pensioners do not remain for another turn.

No. Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital’s starred flag so it is no longer an empire. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest of the last dominated region.
Each firm share’s scoring VP by Value is: Value 1 = −1 VP; 2 = 0; 3–4 = ½; 5–7 = 1; 8–9 = 1½; 10 = 2.

Chairman title holder acts first in Family, then players clockwise. After all family actions, the New Company shares step occurs: if Debt and applicants remain, move rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one, repeating while both remain; if no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible preserving order.

Follow red ribbon: Chairman → Director of Trade (or Governor General) → Manager of Shipping → Military Affairs → Bombay Presidency → Madras Presidency → Bengal Presidency → China Superintendent if created. Skip each vacant office. Inside each Presidency, President chooses order of Commander, Governors and Trade, and each position finishes before next. Each office spends only its own treasury. Offices created by actions go into Vacant Offices unless immediate hiring is specified; new Governorship normally waits for later Hiring.

Begin by rolling storm die; its face specifies affected sea zones and number of India events. Resolve all required storms before drawing events. Then flip and resolve tiles one at a time from draw stack, for as many events as that die face specifies. For an event using a region, normally read the back of the new top tile in the draw stack, not the tile just drawn, subject to the specific event location rule. Company and extra ships never roll storms; player ships in Company fleets check affected zones, China ships count Eastern, firms count strategy zone, and Hobnob firms are exempt.
answers.evidence: Events in India — opening/storm sequence; storm exposure table.

answers.answer: On an ordinary Crisis, Elephant’s tail is attacker/acting region and head is defender. A sovereign actor (large capital flag or unflagged dome) means Invasion; a dominated actor (small flag or no dome) means Rebellion against its sovereign. If Elephant is fully inside a Company region, resolve Rebellion against Company. Sovereign regions are dome without a flag or capital/star flag; dominated regions have a small flag or no dome. This classifier is for ordinary Elephant-located Crisis, while Foreign Invasion uses its own location rule.
answers.evidence: India terminology; Events — Choose the ordinary Crisis procedure from the Elephant.
